4. Artificial intelligence: our commitments under EU law

VF Empire designs and builds artificial intelligence systems. We operate within the European Union and treat the European regulatory framework for AI as an engineering specification.

4.1 The EU Artificial Intelligence Act

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council (the “EU AI Act”) establishes a harmonised, risk-based legal framework for artificial intelligence in the Union. VF Empire commits to the following in the design, development and delivery of its systems:

  • Prohibited practices (Article 5). We do not design, build or deploy AI systems for practices prohibited by the EU AI Act, including manipulative or exploitative techniques causing significant harm, social scoring by or for public authorities, untargeted scraping of facial images for recognition databases, emotion recognition in workplaces or educational institutions (outside legal exemptions), or real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces outside the narrow exceptions provided by law.
  • Risk classification. Every system programme we undertake is assessed against the AI Act’s risk categories before build. Where a commissioned system would qualify as a high-risk AI system (Annex III), we engineer to the corresponding requirements: risk management systems (Article 9), data governance (Article 10), technical documentation (Article 11), record-keeping and logging (Article 12), transparency to deployers (Article 13), human oversight (Article 14), and accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity (Article 15).
  • Human oversight by architecture. VF systems are built around gates: outputs are checked against evidence, and decision authority remains with accountable humans. Supervised autonomy is our default engineering posture, not an optional extra.
  • Transparency (Article 50). Where our systems interact directly with natural persons, they are designed to disclose that the person is interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from context. Where our systems generate or manipulate synthetic content, we support machine-readable marking of such content in accordance with the Act.
  • General-purpose AI models. VF Empire primarily integrates and orchestrates open-source and third-party models rather than placing its own general-purpose AI models on the Union market. Where obligations for providers or deployers of general-purpose AI models (Chapter V) apply to an engagement, they are addressed in the engagement’s technical documentation.
  • AI literacy (Article 4). Our AI Training Centre programmes are designed to advance the AI literacy of the people who operate, deploy and are affected by AI systems.

4.2 Data protection

Our systems are engineered local-first: models, data and controls are designed to run on infrastructure controlled by the system’s owner. Processing of personal data by VF Empire is governed by Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (“GDPR”) and Maltese data protection law, as described in our Privacy Policy. Where VF acts as a processor for a client, a data processing agreement pursuant to Article 28 GDPR forms part of the engagement.

4.3 No guarantee of regulatory outcomes

Statements on this Site about regulatory compliance describe our engineering commitments and methodology. They are not legal advice to you, and they do not guarantee that any particular deployment by a client (whose context, data and use case we may not control) will satisfy the legal obligations that apply to that client. Responsibility for a deployer’s obligations under the EU AI Act, GDPR and other applicable law rests with the deployer.
